claims.objects: An integer secant-number offset h, an integer repair-support size r, and the two rational affine lower bounds used at the end of the characteristic-three argument.
claims.hypotheses: The support is nonempty, and it has size at least two when h is congruent to one modulo three.
claims.conclusion: The maximum of the pair-count bound and the repair-support bound is at least four.
claims.cautions: Lean proves only the final discrete minimization. It does not define the projective plane or arc, import the Szőnyi--Weiner theorem, construct the repaired multiset, prove the support bounds, or carry out the asymptotic reduction.

claims.objects: Positive rational parameters u and v and the manuscript's balanced-integer and real-incidence first-order coefficients.
claims.conclusion: The coefficient difference equals the displayed positive rational factorization.
claims.cautions: Lean does not prove the complete arc bound, the integer minimization defining c_Z, the classification of all rational equality parameters, or any asymptotic localization of the number of n-secants.

claims.objects: The integer secant-number offset and the two pairs of rational affine lower bounds in the odd- and even-offset branches.
claims.hypotheses: The offset is respectively odd or even, expressed by its residue modulo two.
claims.conclusion: The odd branch has coefficient at least 73/6 and the even branch has coefficient at least 37/3.
claims.cautions: Lean proves only the two discrete minimizations. It does not formalize sets of even type, the stability theorem, the generator-line count, or the asymptotic projective-geometric argument.

claims.objects: A finite integer degree sequence with prescribed sum N*a+w and twice the unordered-pair weight z(z-1).
claims.hypotheses: Only the exact sum identity is required; the theorem is valid for integer-valued sequences.
claims.conclusion: The twice-pair sum is at least N*a(a-1)+2aw, which is twice the manuscript's balanced minimum when 0 <= w < N.
claims.cautions: The formal theorem covers the lower balanced bound but not the upper-box filling formula or its equality characterization. The manuscript states the result for nonnegative integer degrees and divides the formal identity by two.

claims.objects: Two integer pair counts, their lower and upper bounds, and a total pair count partitioned between them.
claims.hypotheses: The two actual counts sum to the total and each lies in its declared integer interval.
claims.conclusion: The external interval meets the reflection of the internal interval through the total pair count.
claims.cautions: Lean proves the interval-overlap implication once the pair partition and endpoints are supplied. It does not define symmetric designs, double-count block intersections, or compute heterogeneous integer-box extrema.

claims.objects: A selected block family in a symmetric design and its two point classes.
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the exact integer incidence condition.
claims.conclusion: The standard real incidence inequality and its constant-degree equality condition.
claims.cautions: No Lean declaration currently represents the Cauchy--Schwarz derivation or its equivalence with incidence mixing.

claims.objects: A (k,n)-arc and its internal and external n-secant degrees.
claims.hypotheses: The projective-plane incidence axioms and the n-secant property.
claims.conclusion: The two pencil bounds and the incidence and pair-count identities.
claims.cautions: Finite projective planes, arcs, secants, and their double counts are not defined in this package.

claims.objects: The family of all n-secants of a (k,n)-arc with prescribed external coverage multiplicity.
claims.hypotheses: Every external point is incident with at least lambda n-secants.
claims.conclusion: The stated range for the number of n-secants and the exact integer interval condition.
claims.cautions: The specialization of the abstract arithmetic to projective incidence geometry is not formalized.

claims.objects: Positive rational factors u and v and the associated alpha, beta, lambda, and a.
claims.hypotheses: The factors u and v are positive.
claims.conclusion: The displayed factor-indexed parameters satisfy the two continuous equality equations.
claims.cautions: Lean proves the forward substitution only. It does not prove that every rational solution arises uniquely from an ordered factorization.

claims.objects: The exact balanced pair-count function F(T) along a rational equality family.
claims.hypotheses: Bounded first-order arc coefficient, prescribed external coverage, and F(T) <= 0.
claims.conclusion: The number T of n-secants differs by O(1) from its leading value.
claims.cautions: The floor-sum forward-difference argument and its uniform asymptotic bounds are not formalized.

claims.objects: The rational crossing h_* associated with positive integers u and v.
claims.hypotheses: The manuscript's definitions of h_* and M_0.
claims.conclusion: Integrality of h_* is equivalent to the displayed divisibility condition, with an even diagonal family as a corollary.
claims.cautions: The polynomial division and divisibility cancellation are not formalized.

claims.objects: A dual multiset of n-secants and a finite support on which it is changed to exact modular type.
claims.hypotheses: Characteristic compatibility, external secant coverage, fixed nonzero repair support, and the stated asymptotic parameters.
claims.conclusion: Each repair-support point adds the displayed amount to the first-order lower bound.
claims.cautions: The dual incidence construction, modular residues, and generator-line completeness count are not formalized.

claims.objects: The characteristic-three dual secant multiset with exact one-modulo-three line intersections.
claims.hypotheses: The stated asymptotic form, coefficient below four, and zero repair support.
claims.conclusion: The exact pair identity is impossible.
claims.cautions: The congruence-restricted convex pair-count calculation is checked by the separate exact Python evidence but is not represented in Lean.

claims.objects: The characteristic-two dual n-secant set when the repair set is empty.
claims.hypotheses: Every dual line has even intersection and the stated near-equality parameters.
claims.conclusion: The first-order coefficient is at least sixteen.
claims.cautions: The congruence-restricted pair-count calculation is checked by the separate exact Python evidence but is not represented in Lean.

claims.objects: A nonempty symmetric-difference repair set in characteristic two.
claims.hypotheses: The dual n-secant set differs from a set of even type at r points.
claims.conclusion: Odd and even repair sizes give the stated external-excess bounds, and r, T, and h have the same parity.
claims.cautions: Symmetric differences of projective lines and their external-point counts are not formalized.

claims.hypotheses: The characteristic-three theorem and the standard complement correspondence.
claims.conclusion: The complement is a minimal q/3-fold blocking set with the displayed upper bound.
claims.cautions: Neither the geometric complement dictionary nor the asymptotic theorem is formalized.

claims.objects: A projective linear code, the hyperplanes containing the maximum number of columns, and candidate extension columns.
claims.hypotheses: The standard projective-system representation of the code.
claims.conclusion: The two degree sequences satisfy the exact interval condition in the point--hyperplane design.
claims.cautions: The code/projective-system dictionary and the projective point--hyperplane design are not formalized.
